Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Host-owned JSON mods

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Fresh Solo, Host and Server sessions load user://mods/*.json in filename order. RSY_MODS_DIR overrides the folder. Room followers and clients never read local overlays; they receive the authority's complete value catalog. A resumed game keeps the catalog in its checkpoint. Explicit fixture identities do not implicitly load user mods unless persistence is enabled or a mod directory is specified.

The reader accepts the original JSON5 authoring vocabulary: guns, mobs, status, combos and abilities. Rows replace the entire corresponding entry, so include all gameplay fields. Combination rows append after existing rules; first-match precedence is preserved. Later files replace earlier rows. Each file is validated and committed atomically; malformed or invalid files are reported and skipped.

Example:

JSON
{"guns":[{"id":0,"name":"junkcannon","kind":"bolt","cooldown":20,
"dmg":9,"mag":8,"reload_ticks":72,"jam_per_mille":12,"jam_taps":3,
"speed":16,"ttl":40,"sprite_pos":[32,48],"sprite_size":[32,16]}],
"mobs":[{"id":1,"hp":30,"speed":52,"bite":2,"body_r":26,"scale":2.0}]}

Gun kinds are bolt/rivet/nade/lance/mend; unknown words retain the original bolt fallback. Ability families are lob/cone/nova/buff/zone, with the original lob fallback. Reactions are detonate/transmute/spread, with the original detonate fallback. The original positive minima and damage/jam clamps are retained where compatible with the validated catalog. Values outside Replay's existing simulation bounds are rejected instead of narrowing with integer wraparound.

The current catalog supports 16 gun slots, 8 mob slots, 16 status slots, 16 ability slots and 32 combination rows. Status/ability slot zero is reserved. Sparse IDs are supported: empty holes must be completely zero, references to them are rejected, and the loadout/workshop cycles skip them. Saved preferences for unavailable mod content fall back to available choices while keeping the rest of the profile. New mob IDs use the existing default melee behavior; mods change data, not executable brains or scripts. Existing mob display names remain; additional rows receive a stable generated name.

Parsing is bounded by 256 KiB/file, 32 files, nesting depth 32 and a 4 MiB temporary arena per file. Counts, finite numeric values, integer conversion, references and final catalog validity are checked before commit. Those are declared limits beyond the original unconstrained dynamic tables. Network payloads contain validated catalog values, not filesystem paths or JSON that clients execute.

mod_run.sh gives only the host an ordered overlay set and gives clients decoy files they must ignore. It selects sparse gun/ability IDs through the ordinary buttons, fights with them, compares full worlds, saves, and resumes with no mod reload. mod_migration_run.sh checks the host's altered gun/mob data through planned and crash combat takeover. Native tests also execute the original chain, doubled nova and hostile zone data through the ordinary reducers.

Shell
RSY_ROLE=host RSY_MODS_DIR=/path/to/mods nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/play.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/mod_run.sh
RSY_JITTER=20 RSY_LOSS=1000 RSY_DUPLICATE=1000 nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/mod_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/mod_migration_run.sh

The game content ID is now 0x5253435241503040 because sparse selection and profile validation changed. The catalog's logical layout and stock data fingerprint remain unchanged. Full matched original-act playtests, broader mod-driven network effect scenarios, schema migration and deployment remain roadmap work.
